q: What is driving negative sentiment about AI employment?
answer:
## Verified facts

- In a small LinkedIn poll of 200 professionals, about one quarter said they were worried AI could affect their jobs in the future, and 7% said their role had already been replaced; more than half said AI had made their work easier. [The National](https://www.thenationalnews.com/business/money/2025/08/29/uae-professionals-fear-ai-could-replace-jobs-but-admit-its-made-work-easier/)
- A content writer quoted by *The National* said his employer offered him a choice between finding another job and continuing as a remote freelancer for half his salary. He said he believed AI had reduced content writers’ relevance and negotiating power. [The National](https://www.thenationalnews.com/business/money/2025/08/29/uae-professionals-fear-ai-could-replace-jobs-but-admit-its-made-work-easier/)
- A report cited in September 2026 said 14% of respondents expected AI-related role reductions in the next 12–24 months, down from 31% in the prior year’s survey. [Khaleej Times via Magzter](https://www.magzter.com/stories/newspaper/Khaleej-Times/AI-IS-NOT-KILLING-JOBS-IN-UAE-GCC-BUT-RESHAPING-ROLES-SAYS-REPORT?srsltid=AU7gw4UAKLetHSqKgOo0iGhztMiiBq0q4pyn54fm-rtO5rwiEbYJNr6E)
- Another report says 55% of GCC firms are merging roles as AI adoption grows, while 60% of those surveyed expected very minimal job impacts. [Khaleej Times](https://www.khaleejtimes.com/jobs/ai-impact-uae-jobs-firms-restructure-avoid-layoffs)
- A YouGov survey commissioned by HireRight found that 42% of UAE employers use AI to support promotion decisions, and 31% use AI tools to assist with employee-related decisions. [Khaleej Times](https://www.khaleejtimes.com/business/uae-firms-use-ai-to-decide-promotions-and-layoffs-says-new-report)

## Interpretation

**Judgement:** Negative sentiment appears to be driven less by a certainty of mass layoffs than by the possibility of losing income, status, or bargaining power as employers automate tasks, combine roles, or shift work to lower-paid arrangements. Concern may also be heightened when AI is used in consequential workplace decisions such as promotions or layoffs, because workers may fear being judged by systems they cannot easily understand or influence. The reported statements and polls are indicative, not a population-wide measure of sentiment.

q: Compare G42, EDGE and TII's AI research activity.
answer:
## Verified facts

- **G42:** Its AI activity spans applied AI and national-scale cloud, AI and high-performance computing infrastructure through Core42. G42 also joined Nvidia’s Open Secure AI Alliance, which supports open-weight and open-source models and cybersecurity tools. <https://www.g42.ai/resources/news/g42-launches-core42-deliver-national-scale-enterprise-cloud-and-ai-capabilities> · <https://enterpriseam.com/uae/2026/07/29/g42-joins-nvidias-alliance-for-open-source-ai/>
- **G42’s model work is collaborative:** MBZUAI and G42 launched K2 Think, described by the two organisations as a 32-billion-parameter reasoning system. <https://mbzuai.ac.ae/news-events/news/mbzuai-g42-launch-k2-think-leading-open-source-system-advanced-ai-reasoning>
- **EDGE:** Its Group AI Accelerator is described as a centre of excellence for advancing AI in defence solutions and manufacturing and developing local talent. EDGE is also part of an autonomous-logistics platform effort with TII, Micropolis and SteerAI. <https://www.middleeastainews.com/p/new-ai-accelerator-to-boost-edge> · <https://edgegroup.ae/news/edge-tii-micropolis-and-steerai-deploy-advanced-autonomous-logistics-platform>
- **TII:** The institute’s clearest research focus is developing its Falcon model portfolio. It launched Falcon Perception, a vision-and-language model, and later announced Falcon-Emirati 7B alongside models for speech recognition and Arabic documents. <https://www.tii.ae/news/tii-launches-falcon-perception-new-multimodal-ai-model-helps-machines-see-and-understand-world> · <https://gulfbusiness.com/en/2026/artificial-intelligence/uae-tii-falcon-emirati-arabic-ai-model/>

## Interpretation

**Judgement:** TII shows the strongest direct evidence of model-centred AI research, with multiple Falcon models and capabilities across multimodal, Emirati Arabic, speech and documents. G42’s profile appears broader and more deployment-oriented: applied AI and infrastructure, with some research activity through partnerships such as K2 Think. EDGE’s AI work is the most mission-specific of the three, directed toward defence, manufacturing and autonomous systems; the available sources describe an accelerator and applications more clearly than standalone model research.
